name: University Spine
description:
University Circle was Cleveland's cultural and intellectual center — home to Case Western Reserve University, the Cleveland Clinic, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and a concentration of educational and medical institutions that made the neighborhood one of the most institutionally dense square miles in America. All of those institutions still exist, technically. What they have become is something their founders would not recognize.

Case Western Reserve University was acquired by Tessera CorpoNation in 2158 as part of a broader strategy to secure academic research pipelines for neural interface development. The university's name was preserved — Tessera understands the value of institutional branding — but its research agenda is now entirely aligned with Tessera's product roadmap. The Cleveland Clinic underwent a parallel transformation, absorbed into Helix Biosystems' medical services division in 2163. The Clinic's famous research campus is now a Helix sovereign medical zone where experimental procedures are conducted under proprietary jurisdiction, exempt from whatever remains of medical ethics oversight. The Cleveland Museum of Art, unable to compete with neural-direct experience galleries, was converted into a Vantablack Media production facility in 2171, its permanent collection digitized, archived, and reportedly sold to private collectors whose identities Vantablack declines to disclose.

What connects these institutions is the Spine — a climate-controlled elevated walkway system that links every major building in the district, creating a continuous interior environment that Tessera, Helix, and Vantablack employees can traverse without ever touching the ground-level streets. The Spine is the district's real architecture. Below it, the original streets serve as loading docks, maintenance access, and housing for the service workers who keep the elevated institutions running. The vertical segregation is literal: the people who work in the Spine look down at the people who work beneath it, and the sightline goes only one way because the Spine's windows are one-way smart glass.

sights: The Spine — an elevated climate-controlled walkway connecting every major institution, its smart-glass walls opaque from below
Case Western's original Gothic architecture visible beneath Tessera's carbon-fiber expansion modules, like a church consumed by a laboratory
The Cleveland Clinic's Helix sovereign medical zone — pristine white buildings behind biometric barriers, no windows on the research floors
The former Cleveland Museum of Art, its neoclassical facade now displaying Vantablack Media's shifting holographic projections
Ground-level service housing beneath the Spine — functional, overlooked, deliberately invisible from above
sounds: Climate control in the Spine — the whispered hum of a perfectly regulated environment
Medical transport drones moving between Helix facilities, their navigation pings a constant background rhythm
Tessera research audio — the faint whine of neural interface testing equipment, audible through the walls during calibration cycles
Below the Spine: the noise of a working neighborhood — delivery vehicles, maintenance crews, residents living lives the institutions above have engineered out of view
The silence of the former museum — Vantablack's production facility operates on neural-direct workflows that produce no audible sound
smells: The Spine: filtered, temperature-controlled air with Helix's proprietary 'Clarity' scent profile — clean linen and something meant to enhance cognitive focus
Below the Spine: diesel from delivery vehicles, cooking from service worker housing, and the faint chemical bite of Helix medical waste processing
Tessera's research buildings: ozone and biocompatible polymer, the smell of neural interfaces being manufactured
atmosphere.feel: University Spine feels like walking through a body — the elevated walkway is the nervous system, the institutions are the organs, and the ground-level neighborhoods are the parts the body doesn't think about. Everything above the Spine is designed for productivity, efficiency, and the particular comfort of people whose minds are corporate assets. Everything below is designed to support what's above while remaining invisible. The segregation is architectural, economic, and absolute.

demographics: Above the Spine: approximately 8,000 Tessera, Helix, and Vantablack employees, predominantly Tier 3-4, universally augmented. Below the Spine: approximately 20,000 service workers, maintenance staff, and their families, predominantly Tier 1-2. The two populations share physical space and inhabit different worlds.
economy: Neural interface R&D (Tessera), experimental medicine and biotech (Helix Biosystems), media production (Vantablack). The above-Spine economy is entirely corporate. The below-Spine economy is service-based — food preparation, cleaning, maintenance, delivery — compensated at rates that keep workers functional but never mobile. The three corponations maintain a joint economic zone agreement that standardizes wages below the Spine at levels that are, by pure coincidence, identical across all three employers.
power_structure: Tripartite corporate sovereignty. Tessera controls the university campus. Helix controls the medical campus. Vantablack controls the cultural campus. The Spine itself is jointly administered under a shared governance protocol called the Circle Compact. Ground-level territory is technically under Tollgate infrastructure sovereignty, but Tollgate's presence is minimal — they collect fees and maintain systems, but the three resident corponations effectively control everything.
dangers: Corporate jurisdiction complexity — three overlapping sovereignties create legal ambiguities that are dangerous for anyone without a corporate attorney
Helix medical testing — the sovereign medical zone operates without external oversight, and the below-Spine population is a convenient source of test subjects who have limited legal recourse
Tessera neural research proximity — experimental BCI signals occasionally leak from the research campus, causing interface glitches in anyone within range
Surveillance density — above the Spine is one of the most monitored environments in the corridor, with three corporate security systems operating simultaneously
Below-Spine exploitation — the wage-fixing arrangement keeps service workers in permanent economic stasis with no pathway to above-Spine employment
opportunities: Tessera's research campus is a source of cutting-edge neural interface intelligence — data that's valuable to every fixer and operator in the corridor
Helix's medical capabilities are accessible to those who can pay or trade — including experimental treatments unavailable elsewhere
The below-Spine workforce knows the physical infrastructure of every institution in the district — knowledge that is operationally invaluable
The Circle Compact's joint administration creates bureaucratic gaps between the three sovereignties that can be exploited
story_hooks: A below-Spine maintenance worker has discovered that Helix's medical waste processing facility is not processing waste — it's processing something else entirely, and the chemical signatures match NeoCortex Industries' known protocols
Tessera's research campus has produced a neural interface prototype that its own engineers are afraid of — and the prototype has gone missing somewhere in the Spine

The Cleveland Museum of Art's permanent collection was supposed to be digitized and archived. A below-Spine delivery worker has found evidence that it was never digitized — it was moved, physically, to a location that doesn't appear on any corporate map
frequented_by: Tessera, Helix, and Vantablack employees — the above-Spine population
Service workers who maintain the institutions — the below-Spine population
Operators who need access to corporate research intelligence
Medical tourists seeking Helix experimental treatments
